Cyber Services is a knowledge-based cyber security service provider offering proactive cyber solutions for both domestic and international markets, primarily for large corporations and governments. Cyber Services offers end-to-end cyber security consulting, from information risk assessments that help you benchmark safety measures and shore up weaknesses, to testing that checks for robust defences.
Cyber Services is present on the Hungarian and international markets since 2015. In addition to traditional IT and information security consulting and R & D, Cyber Services provides a holistic, life-cycle management service, which consists of preventive defence, security management, incident treatment, knowledge transfer and educational services, cyber security planning, management, strategic decision support, information sharing and consulting. Cyber Services works with clients across the full cyber security life cycle, helping to design and embed policies and procedures, including incident response planning, training and education.

entityDescription:
Cineon Training was founded in 2016 by a consortium of academics, nuclear industry consultants and media production experts. Consultants from the UK Nuclear Industry identified a need for more effective Human Performance training within nuclear and other sectors. Cineon Training is a collaboration between the University of Exeter and Cineon Productions ltd.

The overall aim of this collaboration has been to augment and enhance immersive human factors training content, developed by Cineon Training, with the research findings from Dr Vine’s team at the University of Exeter.

Using Virtual Reality simulation, in conjunction with more traditional methods, we aim to improve the training of techniques and principles of human factors that are critical for success (risk management, dealing with pressure, team-work, communication).

We utilise an ‘Evidence Based’ approach to the production and application of training content which is a departure from the traditional training techniques deployed by high-risk industries. This approach, which has already been adopted by the aviation industry, is considered more effective due to the fact that it makes use of up to date research and novel training techniques.

entityDescription:
Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. is an interdenominational human rights and aid organization with its place of residence in Constance. The focus of its work is the world-wide support for people in distress. 
Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. provides support for people whose human rights are violated or threatened. Furthermore, the organization provides humanitarian aid for people in distress in form of disaster relief and emergency aid and is committed to a sustainable development cooperation according to the principle of enabling people to help themselves. Satisfying people's basic needs for food, drink, safety and in particular health plays an essential part in the organization's work. The geographical focus of the activities of Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. is Africa. Since march 2017, Sign of HOpe e.V. have been working mainly in Central Eastern Africa, in particular in Ethiopia, North Kenya and Uganda. In the previous 20 years, the major part of our work took place in the region of today's South Sudan.

entityDescription: The Institute of Catalysis (IC) of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences (BAS) was established on 01.04.1983, based on the Laboratory “Kinetics and Catalysis”, which began its activities as early as 1963, and at present it is a leading center for catalytic science in the country and Southeastern Europe. The structure of IC comprises 3 laboratories and a total of 14 research groups inside the laboratories. The Scientific Council of IC consists of 17 scientists.
